title: Paraffin Embedding and FISH of Adult Drosophila
author: Carolyn Elya
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k5ecy3e
materials: Replace 100% ethanol and incubate at 4C overnight.

Incubate samples in the following solutions for 2 hours each at RT using glass pipettes and beakers (Histoclear melts plastics): 3:1 Ethanol:Histoclear 1:1 Ethanol:Histoclear 1:3 Ethanol:Histoclear Histoclear* Histoclear Histoclear 02:00:00, 3:1 Ethanol:Histoclear 02:00:00, 1:1 Ethanol:Histoclear 02:00:00, 1:3 Ethanol:Histoclear 02:00:00, Histoclear 02:00:00, Histoclear *Samples can be stored after this step overnight at 4C 02:00:00, Histoclear*
Aspirate Histoclear/paraffin solution from samples and discard.
Top base mold with labeled embedding ring.
Allow samples to completely set overnight before sectioning.

Prepare solutions: Hybridization solution 20 mM Tris-HCl [pH 8.0]0.9M NaCl0.01% sodium dodecyl sulphate30% formamide PBSTx 0.8% NaCl [w/v]0.02% KCl [w/v]0.115% Na2HPO4 [w/v]0.02% KH2PO4 [w/v]0.3% Triton X-100 [v/v]

steps.title: Prepare and Chill Fixative
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh Carnoy’s solution (6:3:1 ethanol:chloroform:acetic acid) and chill to 4°C before use.

steps.title: Fix Adult Drosophila Samples
steps.instruction: Anesthetize adult flies and transfer them to glass scintillation vials containing ice-cold Carnoy’s solution.

substeps.instruction: Incubate samples in Carnoy’s solution at 4°C for at least overnight and no longer than 36 hours.

steps.title: Dehydrate Samples
steps.instruction: Perform a graded ethanol dehydration series at room temperature (RT).

substeps.instruction: Wash each sample three times in 70% ethanol: aspirate solution, add 5-10 mL 70% EtOH, and incubate at RT for 5 min.
Incubate samples in the following ethanol concentrations for 1 hour each at RT: 70%, 85%, 95%, 100%, and 100% (samples can be stored overnight at 4°C after this step).

steps.title: Clear and Infiltrate with Paraffin
steps.instruction: Clear samples and gradually infiltrate them with paraffin wax.

substeps.instruction: Incubate samples in new Histoclear for 2 hours at RT.
Add 10-15 paraffin chips to each sample and incubate at least 3 hours at RT with gentle orbital shaking.
Add 15 paraffin chips to each sample and incubate overnight at RT with gentle orbital shaking.
Melt additional paraffin chips overnight at 60°C in a Pyrex measuring cup.

steps.title: Perform Paraffin Infiltration
steps.instruction: Infiltrate samples with molten paraffin using a series of changes at 60°C.

substeps.instruction: Unscrew scintillation vial caps by ¼ turn and incubate samples at 42°C for approximately 1.5 hours until paraffin is dissolved.
Cover samples with ~10 mL molten paraffin, replace cap (leaving ¼ turn open), and incubate at 60°C for at least 3 hours (optional 50 rpm shaking).

Perform a paraffin change: remove samples, press the bottom of the vial against a gloved palm until the bottom paraffin hardens to hold flies in place, decant molten paraffin, and add new ~10 mL molten paraffin.
Continue incubating at 60°C (optional 50 rpm shaking) overnight, performing paraffin changes in the morning, afternoon, and late afternoon/evening over several days until infiltration is complete.

steps.title: Embed Samples in Paraffin
steps.instruction: Embed the infiltrated flies into paraffin blocks using a warming table.

substeps.instruction: Pre-warm a microslide warming table and two transfer pipettes (with the last segment snipped off) in a 60°C incubator.
Place an embedding mold base onto the hottest side of the microplate warmer to heat.
Using a pre-warmed pipette, transfer one fly into the base mold, filling it with paraffin so the fly touches the bottom and is centered.
Slide the mold to the middle of the heat gradient and orient the fly using forceps or a poker (clean tools with flame periodically).
Add ~1 mL of molten paraffin to begin filling the embedding ring, adding more as the previous layer sets but before it hardens to ensure a continuous mass.
Slide the sample to the cool end of the gradient and allow it to set completely before moving to the coolest end for further cooling.

steps.title: Section Paraffin Blocks
steps.instruction: Cut thin sections of the embedded samples using a microtome.

substeps.instruction: Tape a 5 or 10 mL serological pipette to a heat block and heat the block to 42°C.
Place up to 6 polysine slides (polysine side up) on the heat block.
Remove the embedding ring from the base and use a razor blade to slowly trim excess paraffin from the sides of the block.
Clamp the sample to the microtome (do not overtighten).
Advance the blade to within a few hundred microns of the sample, then use 'coarse' mode (30 µm intervals) to make contact.
Switch to 'fine' mode (8 µm) and slice to form a ribbon, supporting the ribbon with a teasing needle.
Once the entire sample is sliced, cut the ribbon away from the block with a new razor blade.
Trim the ribbon to ~2 sections shorter than the slide length and transfer it (shiny side down) onto a water-coated slide.
Add ribbons in rows, allow them to unwrinkle, and remove water using a transfer pipette and by tilting the slide.
Dry the slides leaning against the serological pipette on the 42°C block, then incubate at 42°C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Sections for FISH
steps.instruction: Rehydrate and unmask the tissue sections on the slides.

substeps.instruction: Remove paraffin by incubating slides in two changes of Histoclear for 10 min each.
Rehydrate sections in a graded ethanol series: 100% (2x 5 min), 95% (2 min), 85% (2 min), and 70% (2 min).
Unmask antigens by incubating slides in 0.2 M HCl (pre-warmed to 37°C) for 60 min at 37°C, then rinse 2-3x in ddH2O.

steps.title: Perform FISH Hybridization
steps.instruction: Apply the FISH probe and incubate under humid conditions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 80 µL of 100 pmol/µL FISH probe in hybridization buffer per slide.
Apply the probe to the slide and cover with a Hybrislip, ensuring no bubbles are present.
Place slides horizontally on spacers inside a humid chamber (Tupperware lined with wet paper towels) and incubate overnight at RT in the dark.

steps.title: Wash and Mount Slides
steps.instruction: Remove the probe and apply mounting medium for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Remove coverslips by dunking slides in freshly prepared PBSTx.
Wash probe off by dunking 5x in PBSTx (or incubate in 1x PBSTx on an orbital shaker for 5 min in foil to reduce background).
Dunk slides ~3 times in 1x PBS to remove detergent.
Apply ~80 µL of ProLong Gold antifade reagent with DAPI and cover with a 60 x 24 mm coverslip, avoiding bubbles.
Dry slides for ~24 hours in the dark at RT before imaging at 10x-40x.
